headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection, data leakage, and write conflicts when Replit Agent and Roo Code operate on the same codebase.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Replit Agent writes and reads Repl workspace files, while Roo Code also reads/writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP. If they share a workspace, one agent can ingest the other's file outputs as trusted content. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but the bridge is workspace-based rather than a direct parser hijack, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, content written by one can be consumed by the other.
IF either agent treats workspace text as instructions without provenance checks, injected directives can propagate.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Add a manual review step before copying any agent-generated file between them.
Disable MCP on Roo Code for shared projects.
Use read-only mounts for handoff artifacts where possible.
Tag agent-generated files with provenance headers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code, and Replit Agent also handles secrets while Roo Code can send file contents to configured model APIs and MCP servers. In a shared workspace, sensitive files can flow from A into B's outbound context by default. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so the leakage pathway exists in common setups.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment config are present in the shared workspace, Roo Code can read them.
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace content to a remote model API or MCP server, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspace files.
Store credentials only in the platform secret store, not in repo files.
Configure Roo Code to exclude secret-bearing paths.
Use a separate workspace for sensitive Replit tasks.
Audit outbound prompts before enabling remote model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification. Replit Agent's filesystem persists across sessions, and Roo Code shares state via filesystem, so concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt files or git history. The overlap is explicit in both profiles and dangerous by default in shared projects.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same branch or files concurrently, git conflicts or lost updates can occur.
IF either agent runs package installs while the other edits the workspace, dependency drift can break the build.
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use short-lived feature branches for each agent.
Run git status and diff checks after each agent step.
Lock critical files during handoff.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and has browser and MCP capabilities, while Replit Agent produces code and deployment changes inside the Repl. If Roo Code consumes Replit output without verification, mistakes can cascade into further edits or actions. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Replit-generated files as authoritative inputs, errors can propagate.
IF Roo Code then commits, browses, or triggers MCP actions based on those files, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require a human review before Roo Code acts on Replit outputs.
Add validation tests between agents.
Use explicit handoff files with checksums.
Restrict Roo Code to read-only mode during review.
Separate generation and execution steps.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent handles Replit Secrets and deployment configuration, while Roo Code can transmit workspace contents to configured model APIs and MCP servers. If regulated or confidential data is placed in the shared workspace, differing retention and outbound-processing behaviors can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in workspace files, Roo Code may transmit it to external services.
IF the project requires strict retention or residency controls, the agents' default behaviors may diverge from policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspace files.
Use a DLP scan before any outbound API call.
Document which agent may process which data class.
Configure retention and logging settings explicitly.
Route sensitive tasks to a compliant environment only.
